validity.researcher_notes: Building on the annual-update leg already staged for this row (batches/india-gas/staging/annual/rows/P0766.json), which independently confirmed the full spec chain (length, diameter, capacity, fuel source, proposal year, 85/5/5/5 ownership) at high tier and, critically, ran a dedicated status_reviews pass in June 2026 — not re-deriving any of that, just applying it to the endpoint_country question. That status review cites THREE independent, dated 2026 Afghan outlets all reporting active physical pipe-laying specifically inside Afghanistan: Pajhwok Afghan News (2026-05-20, '64km of TAPI pipeline laid in Afghanistan'), Ariana News (2026-06-15, '~84 kilometres... approximately 60 percent complete'), and Kabul Tribune ('52% of TAPI Pipeline Work Completed in Herat') — with no equivalent reports found (there or here) of construction activity inside Pakistan or India. Given that, a drawn route whose last endpoint lands in Afghanistan (31.717, 65.715 — consistent with the pipeline's real corridor through southern Afghanistan toward the Pakistan border near Kandahar, not an implausible location) plausibly reflects the portion of the route that is physically real/under active construction as of the most recent evidence, while the unbuilt Pakistan and India legs (Quetta-Multan-Fazilka) were never drawn. This matches the endpoint_country flag's explicit 'may be a correctly-drawn partial route' case for a transit pipeline stopping in Afghanistan. I am not proposing new coordinates to extend the geometry through Pakistan into India, since no independent source describes construction or a finalized route there yet — doing so would be fabricating geometry for an unbuilt segment, which is out of scope.
